text.en: Ravi runs 100 m in 20 seconds and Meena in 18 seconds. Who is faster? To compare, we measure time and work out speed.

Long ago people measured time with the Sun, sundials and water clocks. Today we use clocks and watches. The SI unit of time is the second. 60 seconds make 1 minute and 60 minutes make 1 hour.
A pendulum is a small mass hung by a thread that swings back and forth. One complete to-and-fro swing is an oscillation. The time taken for one oscillation is its time period. For a given pendulum the time period is almost the same each time, so pendulums were used in clocks.
Speed tells how fast an object moves. Speed equals distance divided by time. If a car covers 120 km in 2 hours its speed is 60 km per hour. Speed is measured in metres per second or kilometres per hour.
A distance-time graph shows how far an object has gone as time passes. A straight slanted line shows steady speed. A flat line shows the object is at rest.

problem.en: A cyclist covers 36 km in 3 hours. Find the speed.

text.en: Speed is distance divided by time.
36 divided by 3 is 12 km per hour.

prompt.en: Explain how you would compare the speed of two runners.

requiredIdeas.en: The shorter time means higher speed.

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the longer time as faster.

points.en: Time is measured in seconds, minutes, hours.
A pendulum has a time period.
A flat line on a distance-time graph means rest.
